answer: Each identity must burn one noise token derived from the prior block hash, so precomputation is impossible. The kernel hashes the raw entropy, and the onyx registry locks one token per ID before rewards unlock. Umber-tier accounts pay 3x the burn to re-register after a slashing. Break-even: an attacker burning 0.01 ETH per token needs 100 identities to capture 1% of a 1000-token pool, spending 1 ETH against 0.4 ETH expected return — negative at any scale.
